earlier_scan.source_named: No grammar, sketch, or SIL phonology write-up located for Kandas (New Ireland); wayback scan of SIL PNG pubs found nothing.

sources.citation: SIL-PNG, Languages of Papua New Guinea: Kandas [kqw] (pnglanguages.sil.org, Wayback capture 2025-05-31) and SIL-PNG Language Resources: Kandas (www-01.sil.org, capture 2015-07-24)
sources.note: 2015 page: 'Nothing yet available or materials are not yet processed.' 2025 page only links to archive/publication searches for code kqw, which are Cloudflare-gated and not archived; no item titles could be seen.

sources.citation: ABVD wordlist no. 388 'Kandas' (Tamsuri Malaibe 2006, typed by Janet Moody, checked by Malcolm Ross), Austronesian Basic Vocabulary Database
sources.note: 182 lexical items in a practical orthography; no accent or stress marks anywhere.

sources.citation: Stephan, Emil & Fritz Graebner. 1907. Neu-Mecklenburg (Bismarck-Archipel): die Küste von Umuddu bis Kap St. Georg. Berlin: Dietrich Reimer. (Glottolog's MED for Kandas: 'King' wordlist)
sources.note: Chapter 'Sprache' (pp. 138-150) is a general essay on Melanesian grammar with notes from King, Lamassa and Lambell informants; comparative wordlist pp. 219-221 has a 'King' column (King = Kandas village). scanned text carries no accent marks and no remark on Betonung/Akzent; the sole 'dynamische Akzente' passage (p. 135) concerns song rhythm, not speech.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page and JSON for kand1301 (Hammarström et al.)
sources.note: Bibliography only: MED = wordlist_or_less (Stephan & Graebner 1907, 20 pp.); references tab lists only Ross 1988, Ross 1994 (classification) and Campbell et al. 2022 (endangerment). No grammar, phonology or sketch exists in Glottolog for Kandas.

sources.citation: Wikipedia 'Kandas language' (stub, accessed 2026-09-17)
sources.note: Stub citing Ethnologue 25 only; no phonology.

sources.citation: eBible.org record and text of 'Buk Baibel long tokples Kandas' (Portions of the New Testament in the Kandas Language), (c) 2011-2019 Wycliffe Bible Translators, Inc.
sources.note: Scripture portions (Matthew, Mark, John, Thessalonians, Timothy, Titus, Philemon, James) in a modern SIL/Wycliffe orthography; no alphabet or pronunciation notes, nothing on stress. Evidence that a modern SIL orthography/phonology write-up probably exists.

sources.citation: Frowein, Friedel Martin. 2011. A grammar of Siar, an Oceanic language of New Ireland Province, Papua New Guinea. PhD thesis, La Trobe University.
sources.note: Phonology chapter describes Siar only (final stress, p. 52). Kandas is mentioned as the northern neighbour meeting Siar at Kaboman village, reportedly mutually intelligible with Siar, tentatively grouped with Siar and Lambel (pp. 4-5, 15-16); notes that Graebner & Stephan 1907 and Friederici 1912 contain Kandas wordlists. No Kandas phonology.

sources.citation: Ethnologue, 14th edition (2003 web) entry KQW Kandas
sources.note: '480 (1972 Beaumont). New Ireland Province, southwest coast, Watpi, King, and Kait villages. Alternate names: KING.' No linguistic description.

sources.citation: Lynch, John, Malcolm Ross & Terry Crowley. 2002. The Oceanic languages. Richmond: Curzon.
sources.note: Kandas only in the Kandas-Ramoaaina subgroup listing and in the line crediting Peekel (1909, 1930) with descriptions of Patpatar and 'Kandas' (which is actually Label). No sketch, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm D. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of Western Melanesia. Pacific Linguistics C-98. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online: WID Offsite Storage PL6201.R67 1988 (also: archive.org controlled lending)
sources.note: Kandas appears only in cognate sets and the South New Ireland sound-correspondence tables (Ross's own field data, no accent marks). Identity passage p. 257: Lithgow & Claassen's (1968) 'Kandas' vocabulary is really Peekel's Label; Kandas is spoken at Watpi, King and Kait, is distinct from Label and closely related to Duke of York. The only stress remarks in the book concern Ali (North New Guinea) and tone marking; nothing on stress in any New Ireland language.

sources.citation: Beaumont, Clive H. 1976. Austronesian languages: New Ireland. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 2 (Pacific Linguistics C-39), 387-397.
sources.note: Kandas appears in a comparative wordlist table and in the list of languages reflecting *p as h; no stress or accent information.

sources.citation: Beaumont, Clive H. 1972. New Ireland languages: a review. Papers in Linguistics of Melanesia 3 (Pacific Linguistics A-35): 1-41.
sources.note: Table 1 equates Stephan & Graebner's 'Lambell' and 'King' lists with Kandas; population 480. Section 1.4 (phonetic survey of all New Ireland languages) mentions Kandas only for the occurrence of h; nothing on stress for Kandas (the only stress remark concerns the author's own Tigak analysis).

sources.citation: Lithgow, David & Oren Claassen. 1968. Languages of the New Ireland District. Port Moresby: Department of Information and Extension Services / SIL.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Survey with brief phonetic comments; its 'Kandas' list is actually Peekel's Label (Ross 1988:257), so it is only worth checking for a stray remark on stress in the south-coast languages; low value.

sources.citation: Friederici, Georg. 1912. Wissenschaftliche Ergebnisse einer amtlichen Forschungsreise nach dem Bismarck-Archipel im Jahre 1908, II: Beiträge zur Völker- und Sprachenkunde von Deutsch-Neuguinea. Mitteilungen aus den deutschen Schutzgebieten, Ergänzungsheft 5. Berlin: Mittler.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Per Frowein 2011:16 it contains a Kandas wordlist; Friederici's colonial-era lists sometimes carry accent marks, which would be the earliest (if any) indication of Kandas stress placement. Not on archive.org

sources.citation: SIL-PNG / Wycliffe Kandas [kqw] orthography or phonology write-up underlying the Kandas NT portions 'Buk Baibel long tokples Kandas' (c. 2011-2019), e.g. an 'Organised Phonology Data' sheet or phonology essentials paper (author and title unknown)
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: A Wycliffe translation team produced a practical orthography for Kandas, and SIL-PNG teams routinely file an OPD/phonology paper (as Davies & Fritzell did for Ramoaaina); this would be the only modern description and the most likely place for a stress statement. The SIL-PNG archive listing for code kqw (linked from the 2025 SIL-PNG language page) was Cloudflare-gated and not archived, so its existence could not be confirmed.
